goals.0: The password is right in the page source.
goals.1: Right-click is blocked by JavaScript — but only in a browser.
goals.2: The page loads an image from a browsable /files/ directory.
goals.3: Even Google won't find this one — but robots.txt talks.
goals.4: Access is granted only to visitors referred from the natas5 site.
goals.5: Login state lives in a cookie you control.
goals.6: The source code reveals a secret stored in an include file.
goals.7: An include parameter is used without any validation.
goals.8: The secret is 'encoded' in the source: bin2hex(strrev(base64(x))). Encoding is not encryption.
goals.9: A search form feeds your input straight into a grep command.
goals.10: Same form, but ; | & are filtered now. Spaces and grep's file arguments are not.
goals.11: The 'data' cookie is base64 of a repeating-key XOR of known JSON — recover the key and forge an admin cookie.
goals.12: An upload form keeps your file's .php extension.
goals.13: The upload now checks the file type with exif_imagetype — so make the PHP look like a GIF.
goals.14: A login form builds its SQL query with your username inside it.
goals.15: The form only says whether a user exists — a blind SQL injection oracle. Brute-force the password through it.
goals.16: The dictionary search filters shell metacharacters but not $() command substitution — turn it into a yes/no oracle and extract the password character by character.
goals.17: Same injectable user check as before, but every line of output is commented out — the only remaining channel is response time.
goals.18: Admin login is disabled, but sessions are numbered with rand(1, 640) — try every session id until you find the admin's live session.
goals.19: Session ids are now hex-encoded '<number>-<username>' strings — forge candidate ids for the username 'admin' and find the live one.
goals.20: A custom session handler stores each key as a raw 'key value' line — smuggle a newline into your name and you can write extra keys into your own session.
goals.21: Two colocated sites share one session store; the harmless-looking style experimenter writes any submitted field into the session — including 'admin'.
goals.22: The answer is sent and then hidden behind a redirect — read the redirect response itself instead of following it.
goals.23: The password check mixes a substring test with a numeric comparison — PHP's loose typing lets one string be both.
goals.24: The login compares your input with strcmp() — feed it an array and the comparison errors out in your favor.
goals.25: A 'safe' include strips ../ and bans the password path by name — but it logs your User-Agent to an includable file, and the strip itself can be folded back into a traversal.
goals.26: A drawing cookie is unserialized without checks — inject a crafted object whose destructor writes a file of your choosing.
goals.27: Registration truncates names to 64 characters while the data dump trims them — a padded lookalike account makes the dump hand you the real user's row.
goals.28: The query is escaped and then ECB-encrypted into the backend SQL — cut ciphertext blocks from a donor query and splice in an unescaped UNION SELECT.
goals.29: A Perl open() treats the chosen 'file' as a shell pipeline — and the one word the filter bans can be smuggled past it inside shell quotes.
goals.30: The login quotes parameters 'safely' — unless a parameter arrives twice, which silently switches quote() into its unquoted numeric mode.
goals.31: A CSV viewer reads lines from a user-named handle — name it ARGV and the 'file' it iterates is your URL, pipe and all.
goals.32: Same ARGV flaw, one twist: the flag file is unreadable, so run the privileged helper binary the level provides instead of reading the file.
goals.33: A firmware uploader executes any file whose MD5 matches a stored signature — and a Phar archive lets you forge the object that carries both.
